population.span: Patients with type 2 diabetes who were at high risk for cardiovascular disease were randomly assigned, in a 1:1 ratio, to receive liraglutide or placebo.

endpoint.span: The primary composite outcome in the time-to-event analysis was the first occurrence of death from cardiovascular causes, nonfatal (including silent) myocardial infarction, or nonfatal stroke.

estimate.span: The primary composite outcome occurred in fewer patients in the liraglutide group (608 of 4668 patients [13.0%]) than in the placebo group (694 of 4672 [14.9%]) (hazard ratio, 0.87; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.78 to 0.97;

analysis_set.span: All the patients who underwent randomization were included in the primary and exploratory analyses,

treatment_strategy.span: patients were randomly assigned, in a 1:1 ratio, to receive either 1.8 mg (or the maximum tolerated dose) of liraglutide or matching placebo once daily as a subcutaneous injection in addition to standard care

follow_up.span: The median follow-up was 3.8 years in each group.

entry_population_matches_question.why: Participants were adults with type 2 diabetes and high cardiovascular risk; all randomized patients were included in the primary analysis.

notes: All fields use the held full text. Entry criteria required age 50 or older with cardiovascular coexisting disease, or age 60 or older with cardiovascular risk factors. The served HR and CI match the primary three-component outcome, which includes silent myocardial infarction.
